newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Fifteen die in Sierra Leone airport fighting.
newsitem.headline: Fifteen die in Sierra Leone airport fighting.

text.p: Fifteen people, most of them civilians, have been killed during fighting over the past two days around Sierra Leone's international airport at Lungi, outside the capital Freetown, medical sources said on Friday.
The sources at Lungi hospital said that many people had fled the town to escape the fighting.

Residents on Friday said there had been further heavy fighting around the airport town overnight between Nigerian-led West African ECOMOG forces and Sierra Leone troops, backed by rebels who have rallied to the ruling army junta.
Neighbouring West African states are putting pressure on the junta to restore civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who was ousted in a coup on May 25.
Diplomatic talks broke down on July 31, although an earlier round of talks had led to a ceasefire.

Sierra Leone army chiefs would not confirm the fighting overnight, and maintained that their troops had pulled back from the airport area after being shelled by the ECOMOG forces in the early hours of Thursday.
Sierra Leone chief of army staff Nelson Williams told reporters on Friday: "Our troops are now 2-1/2 miles from the airport."
On Thursday, Brigadier Samuel Koroma, brother of junta leader Johnny Paul Korona, said the Sierra Leone forces had withdrawn some 35 miles (some 20 km) from the airport.
A senior member of the junta, who requested anonymity, told Reuters: "We don't want the Nigerians at the airport. We will continue to harass them to leave there."
The ECOMOG high command issued a statement late on Thursday accusing the junta troops of breaking the ceasefire and launching an attack on its soldiers on Wednesday night.
"(The junta) and its cohorts have violated the ceasefire by its unwholesome actions against ECOMOG troops and the innocent citizens of Sierra Leone," it said.
Foreign ministers from Nigeria, Ghana, Ivory Coast and Guinea were continuing talks in the Ghanaian capital, Accra, on Friday to consider their next step.
